summary: Audit all 2026-08-11 changes + recorded evidence for the robot shaking root cause

confirmed.title: A-button exit from motion mode bypasses the mode blend — one-step snap remains
confirmed.detail: The patches blend the Y-press and stale-VR exits (switch_to_velocity_mode captures mode_blend_from_real), but handle_low_state calls enable_velocity_policy() on any A edge with no mode guard, and enable_velocity_policy has NO blend capture. Pressing A while tracking in motion mode switches to velocity and snaps the commanded target from the tracked pose to the velocity default pose in one control step — exactly the lunge class the 2026-08-11 patches were written to eliminate. enable_velocity_policy also does not clear an in-flight mode_blend_t0/mode_blend_from_real, so a stale blend from a prior switch can keep blending from an old pose after A. reset_counters (called by enable_velocity_policy) clears the slew anchor, so even an enabled slew limiter will not soften this snap (first tick after reset passes through unclamped).
confirmed.evidence: policy_runtime.py:164-165 (A handled with only robot_state_ready guard, even when current_policy_mode=='motion'); policy_runtime.py:197-212 (enable_velocity_policy: no mode_blend capture, no clear of mode_blend_t0); policy_runtime.py:308-315 (reset_counters clears _slew_prev_target, making the next tick unclamped); contrast policy_runtime.py:214-222 (switch_to_velocity_mode does capture the blend).
confirmed.note: CONFIRMED on all points against /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/HoloMotion/deployment/unitree_g1_ros2_29dof/src/humanoid_policy/policy_runtime.py. (1) A edge at lines 164-165 is guarded only by robot_state_ready — no policy_enabled/mode guard (B at 167-173 and Y at 175-181 both have them), and robot_state_ready stays True during POLICY since set_robot_state never handles "POLICY". (2) enable_velocity_policy (197-212) captures no mode_blend_from_real and leaves mode_blend_t0 untouched (also skips clear_vr_reference_cache, unlike switch_to_velocity_mode at 214-239 which captures the blend at 218-222). (3) First post-A step runs with is_motion=False (soft-start off) and normally mode_blend_t0=None, so commanded target jumps from tracked pose to velocity_default+action*scale in one step — same lunge class the 2026-08-11 blend patch fixed for Y/stale-VR exits. (4) reset_counters (308-317) nulls _slew_prev_target, and apply_policy_output lines 637-638 seed the anchor without clamping, so even an enabled slew limiter passes the first post-A target through unclamped (slew defaults to 0 anyway). (5) Stale-blend sub-claim is true as code behavior but lower severity: an in-flight blend (<HOLOMOTION_MODE_BLEND_S=1.5s) continues from the old pose across A; older ones self-clear harmlessly at 608-611. Refutations attempted and failed: remote_controller_filter does no button gating; policy_node_29dof.py:986 forwards low-state unconditionally; the control FSM (fsm_sim.py:213) consumes A only in MOVE_TO_DEFAULT, and _send_policy (fsm_sim.py:272-287) forwards targets verbatim at full kp with no smoothing/torque limiting; tests cover A only from idle (test_a_button_enables_velocity_without_vr_reference), never A during motion mode. Suggested fix: guard the A edge (not policy_enabled, or route to switch_to_velocity_mode when mode=='motion') or add blend capture/clear to enable_velocity_policy.

confirmed.title: All three patches decouple the published target from the policy's last_action observation (deliberate, but unbounded and untelemetered)
confirmed.detail: Soft-start, blend, and slew all modify the published target AFTER state.actions_onnx is stored, and the observation pipeline feeds the RAW actions back to the policy as last_action (observation_evaluator._get_obs_last_action returns self.actions_onnx, which the port property resolves to state.actions_onnx). During the 2.5 s soft-start the robot is pinned near the default pose while the policy observes joint positions that contradict the actions it believes were applied — an out-of-distribution regime for the RL policy that can drive action windup (policy escalates output because the plant 'ignores' it), and with slew enabled the mismatch persists for as long as the raw target exceeds the rate cap. The comments acknowledge the invariant choice, but there is no bound or telemetry on the applied-vs-raw discrepancy, so windup would be invisible until it manifests as a lunge when the ramp expires (alpha/beta reach 1 while actions are saturated high).
confirmed.evidence: policy_runtime.py:556 (np.copyto(actions_onnx, actions) before all shaping), 567-579 (alpha scales target only), 598-616 (blend on target_real only), 617-639 (slew on target_real only); observation_evaluator.py:982-983 (_get_obs_last_action returns self.actions_onnx); policy_node_29dof.py:434-436 (actions_onnx property resolves to runtime state); gpu path passes the same raw array as last_action at policy_runtime.py:513.
confirmed.note: CONFIRMED at the code level; risk mechanism partially weakened. Every citation is accurate: policy_runtime.py:556 stores raw actions before all shaping (soft-start 567-579 scales target_dof_pos_onnx only; blend 598-616 and slew 618-639 shape target_real only); the published value is the shaped target. The observation path feeds raw actions back: observation_evaluator.py:982-983 returns self.actions_onnx, which (evaluator sets no such attribute) delegates via __getattr__ (line 31) to the node property at policy_node_29dof.py:434-436 → state.actions_onnx; GPU path passes the same buffer at policy_runtime.py:513. Stronger than stated: both model configs feed actor_last_action with history_length=context_length, so an entire history window of raw actions is contradicted during shaping, and _get_obs_actor_last_action (obs_eval:859) wires the CPU path. "Unbounded" holds (no clipping in deployment; training clip_actions=100.0 is no practical bound). "Untelemetered" holds (publishers: action/kps/kds/policy_mode/reference only; no raw-action topic, no log/metric of applied-vs-raw anywhere, so the delta is unreconstructable from telemetry). Slew is actually ENABLED on the robot: scripts/start_teleop_container.sh:19 sets HOLOMOTION_TARGET_SLEW_RAD_S=15 (code default 0), contradicting HANDOFF's "DEFAULT OFF on robot". WEAKENED: (1) "lunge when the ramp expires" implies a discontinuity that does not exist — alpha is a continuous smoothstep, so exposure grows smoothly over the 2.5 s, and on-robot slew=15 rad/s caps lunge rate (not amplitude); blend (1.5 s) expires before soft-start (2.5 s). (2) Windup is a hypothesis with counter-evidence: bench/simsmoke/run_smoke.py scenario_b_press_and_track drives the real ONNX policy through soft-start entry + squats in MuJoCo and passes (HANDOFF: suite-validated; slew=8 DID cause 8 falls, 15 passed) — though the suite enters tracking near stand pose, so the worst case (large operator-pose offset at B-press) is untested, and the suite measures falls, not discrepancy. (3) Mismatch starts clean, not from stale state: actions_onnx and KV cache are zeroed at mode entry (policy_runtime.py:277, reset_counters 316-317). Key files: /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/HoloMotion/deployment/unitree_g1_ros2_29dof/src/humanoid_policy/{policy_runtime.py, observation_evaluator.py, policy_node_29dof.py}, /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/scripts/start_teleop_container.sh, /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/bench/simsmoke/run_smoke.py, /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/HoloMotion/checkpoints/holomotion_v1.4/config.yaml.

confirmed.title: NaN action targets are logged but still published to the control node
confirmed.detail: Outside the audited patches but directly downstream of them: _publish_action_target checks np.isnan(...).any(), logs 'Action contains NaN values', and then publishes the message anyway (msg.data was already filled before the check, and publish is unconditional). Combined with the env-parse weakness below, or any NaN from the ONNX session, NaN joint targets reach /humanoid/action and whatever the (freshly restored stock) humanoid_control binary does with them. There is no early return, hold-last-good, or e-stop trigger.
confirmed.evidence: policy_node_29dof.py:1370-1381 — 'action_msg.data = target_dof_pos_real.tolist()' precedes the NaN check; 'self.action_pub.publish(action_msg)' executes regardless of the check outcome. File has no .orig, i.e. this is shipped behavior, not a local patch.
confirmed.note: CONFIRMED — every refutation attempt failed; the finding is accurate and slightly understated. (1) Cited code verified verbatim at /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/HoloMotion/deployment/unitree_g1_ros2_29dof/src/humanoid_policy/policy_node_29dof.py:1370-1381: action_msg.data = target_dof_pos_real.tolist() (line 1375) precedes the np.isnan(...).any() check (1378), which only logs 'Action contains NaN values' (1379); self.action_pub.publish(action_msg) at 1381 is unconditional. No early return, hold-last-good, or e-stop. The publisher targets robot_config.action_topic = '/humanoid/action' (src/config/g1_29dof_holomotion.yaml:5). Path is live: policy_runtime.py:539 -> publish_current_action (644) -> port._publish_action_target (645). (2) No upstream sanitization: grep over humanoid_policy/*.py shows zero isnan/isfinite/nan_to_num between ONNX output and publish (the only isfinite guards are on reference qpos ingest and offline conversion, not policy output). Worse: the mode-blend and slew-limit math in policy_runtime.py (~600-645) propagate NaN, and the slew limiter's np.copyto(prev, target_real) poisons _slew_prev_target, so one NaN frame makes all subsequent frames clip against NaN bounds and stay NaN even if the policy recovers — a persistence amplifier the finding didn't mention. (3) Downstream stock controller does NOT save it: in src/src/main_node.cpp PolicyActionHandler (~695-740), the joint-limit gate is 'if (calculated_pos < min_pos || calculated_pos > max_pos)' — both comparisons are false for NaN under IEEE-754, so std::clamp at 734 is skipped and NaN lands in target_dof_pos; SendPolicyCommand (~589-638) writes it straight into low_command.motor_cmd[].q on /lowcmd with no isnan/isfinite anywhere in the file (size mismatch e-stops, NaN does not). (4) The main_node.cpp .orig diff is only the 26-line L1 damped-e-stop patch; the NaN passthrough is identical in the stock version, so the 'freshly restored stock binary' behaves the same. (5) policy_node_29dof.py has no .orig, no uncommitted diff vs git HEAD (single commit e0335fa) — committed/shipped behavior, not a local patch. Net effect: a single NaN from the ONNX session or env parsing reaches motor q targets under full policy kp (no torque limiting in SendPolicyCommand), and the slew-state poisoning makes it sticky. Suggested fix: early-return + hold-last-good (and optionally trigger the damped e-stop) in _publish_action_target, plus an isfinite gate in PolicyActionHandler.

confirmed.title: Supervisor connection-watch node bounce is dead code: ss column off by one
confirmed.detail: run_rehearsal_supervised.sh lines 85 and 93 parse peer addresses with `ss -tn state established '( sport = :63901 )' | ... awk '{print $5}'`. When a state filter is given, ss OMITS the State column, so the peer address is field 4 and field 5 is the Process column, which is empty without -p. CONNS/CONNS_PREV are therefore always empty strings, NEW_PEER never fires, and the entire 'bounce node on new app connection' feature (lines 94-104) has never executed. Consequence: an operator hitting Send/reconnect is not picked up 'immediately' as designed; recovery instead falls through to the stall path, which after the 'timestamps FROZEN' re-arm (line 119 sets SEEN_DATA=0, line 126 sets THRESH=90) can take up to ~90 seconds. Fix: awk '{print $4}' (or drop the state filter).
confirmed.evidence: Verified on this machine: `ss -tn state established` header is 'Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port Peer Address:Port Process' (no State column) vs `ss -tn` which has 5 data columns. /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/scripts/run_rehearsal_supervised.sh:85, :93.
confirmed.note: CONFIRMED by live end-to-end test, not just header inspection. On this machine (iproute2-5.15.0), `ss -tn state established` omits the State column (header: Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port Peer Address:Port Process), so the peer address is awk field 4. Opened a real TCP connection to the actually-listening PC service on 127.0.0.1:63901 and ran the exact pipeline from run_rehearsal_supervised.sh lines 85/93: the $5 pipeline returned ' ' (empty — zero loop items), while a $4 pipeline returned '[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:34406' (the real peer). Therefore CONNS/CONNS_PREV are always empty, NEW_PEER (only assigned at lines 95-97) never fires, and the bounce branch (lines 99-104) is unreachable dead code. Consequence also checks out: recovery falls to the stall path where THRESH is 12 s normally but 90 s whenever SEEN_DATA=0 (line 119 re-arms it on head_pose_dead/timestamps FROZEN; line 126 applies the 90 s grace), so a reconnect can take up to ~90 s instead of the intended immediate bounce. Fix verified: awk '{print $4}' extracts the peer correctly under the state filter; dropping the state filter would also make $5 correct (plain ss -tn has 5 data columns with State first). File: /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/scripts/run_rehearsal_supervised.sh:85,93. No refutation found.

confirmed.title: SIGTERM is ignored while node waits for body data, forcing SDK-slot-leaking SIGKILL
confirmed.detail: main() installs the stop_event signal handlers (line 1074) and then calls init_xrt (line 1075), whose 'waiting for body data' loop (lines 1014-1041) never checks stop_event — it loops on xrt.is_body_data_available() forever. The signal handler runs and returns; the loop continues. The supervisor's graceful_kill sends SIGTERM, waits only 3 s, then SIGKILLs (script lines 26-30). But supervisor-initiated restarts happen precisely when no body data is flowing, i.e., when the node is most likely parked in this loop — so in practice restarts during the no-data phase escalate to SIGKILL, which per the script's own comment (lines 21-23) 'leaks the PC-service SDK client slot (one client max!) and the next node connects but never receives body data'. This can silently convert one stall into a persistent dataless state until the service is recycled. Fix: check the stop_event in init_xrt's loop (pass it in, or make it module-visible) and exit cleanly with xrt.close().
confirmed.evidence: /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/HoloMotion/deployment/holomotion_teleop/holomotion_teleop_node.py:1012-1041 (loop with no stop check), :1074-1075; /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/scripts/run_rehearsal_supervised.sh:19-31 (3 s TERM->KILL escalation, comment documenting the slot leak).
confirmed.note: CONFIRMED. All refutation attempts failed. (1) Handler (holomotion_teleop_node.py:385-394) only sets a threading.Event and returns, for SIGTERM and SIGINT; per PEP 475 the time.sleep(1) at line 1040 auto-resumes after the handler, so the init_xrt wait loop (1014-1041) — whose sole exit is xrt.is_body_data_available() — continues. Ctrl+C/SIGINT is swallowed too (worse than claimed). (2) main() installs handlers at 1074 then blocks in init_xrt at 1075; xrt.close() lives only in HoloRetargetTeleopNode.stop() (823-824), unreachable while parked pre-construction. (3) Supervisor (run_rehearsal_supervised.sh) does hit this window: with --skip-start-service the wait loop still runs; dataless phase gets 90 s grace (line 126) or only 12 s if SEEN_DATA=1 carried over, then graceful_kill (129) → TERM ignored 3 s → SIGKILL (30). (4) The slot-leak premise is the script's own documented field behavior (lines 11-14, 20-23); one tension: line 101 deliberately uses kill -9 on new-app-connection, so the leak may not be fully deterministic (or line 101 is the same bug again) — nuances severity, not mechanism. Aggravating detail missed by the finding: if the leaked state leaves head_pose_ok printing, the supervisor explicitly refuses to recycle the service (146, 169-171), so the dataless state persists indefinitely with a misleading app-side diagnosis. Fix is sound; also call xrt.close() on the early-exit path since node.stop() is unreachable there. Minor nit: comment is at lines 20-23, not 21-23.

confirmed.title: NEW_PEER bounce path uses raw kill -9, contradicting the script's own SIGKILL-leaks-slot rule
confirmed.detail: The new-app-connection handler kills the node with `kill -9 "$NODE"` (line 101) instead of graceful_kill, so the node's SIGTERM handler never runs stop() -> xrt.close(). graceful_kill's comment (lines 21-23) states a SIGKILL leaks the single PC-service SDK client slot and leaves the next node connected-but-deaf. This path is currently masked by the ss column bug (finding 1) — but fixing that bug alone will make every app reconnect leak the slot, i.e., the reconnect handler would cause exactly the failure it was written to solve. Fix both together: $4 in awk AND graceful_kill on line 101.
confirmed.evidence: /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/scripts/run_rehearsal_supervised.sh:101 (`kill -9 "$NODE"`) vs :19-31 (graceful_kill and its rationale).
confirmed.note: CONFIRMED after adversarial checks. (1) scripts/run_rehearsal_supervised.sh:101 uses raw `kill -9 "$NODE"` while graceful_kill (lines 19-31) exists precisely because SIGKILL leaks the single PC-service SDK client slot. (2) The cleanup skipped by -9 is real: holomotion_teleop_node.py installs a SIGTERM handler (line 392) whose stop_event leads to finally -> node.stop() -> xrt.close() (lines 812-826), and close_xrt_on_stop is True in the real run path (enable_io defaults True at line 483; only fake paths pass False). (3) Masking verified empirically on this host (iproute2-5.15.0): with the `state established` filter ss drops the State column, so the peer address is $4 and $5 is empty — CONNS is always empty, NEW_PEER never fires, and line 101 is currently dead code; fixing only the awk column would activate the SIGKILL leak on every app reconnect. Nuance: the leaked slot can eventually self-heal via the wedge-recycle path (lines 144-153), but only after multiple 90s dataless cycles plus a forced operator reconnect/Mode reset — the exact disruption the handler was meant to prevent. Fix must couple $4 in both ss/awk pipelines (lines 85 and 93) with graceful_kill on line 101.

confirmed.title: flock fd 200 leaks into the viewer and the setsid PC-service fallback — orphan can lock out all future supervisors
confirmed.detail: The lock is held on fd 200 (line 13). The node launch correctly closes it with 200>&- (line 78), but the viewer launch (lines 58-59) and the setsid/nohup runService.sh fallback (lines 159-160) do not — both inherit fd 200 and co-hold the flock. If the supervisor dies while the viewer survives (e.g., killed by `kill` rather than Ctrl+C, so the backgrounded viewer is not signaled), or after the fallback service path has ever run (setsid+nohup makes it survive everything), every future supervisor invocation hits `flock -n 200 || exit` and prints 'another instance holds the lock — exiting' — and since it exits before restart_viewer's pkill, nothing ever clears the holder. The fallback-service case is a permanent lockout until someone manually kills RoboticsServiceProcess. Fix: add 200>&- to both spawn lines.
confirmed.evidence: /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/scripts/run_rehearsal_supervised.sh:13-14 (lock), :58-59 (viewer, no 200>&-), :159-160 (setsid service, no 200>&-), :78 (node correctly gets 200>&-). The script's own comment at :73-74 documents this exact hazard for the node but the other two children were missed.
confirmed.note: CONFIRMED by code inspection and empirical reproduction. All cited lines in /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/scripts/run_rehearsal_supervised.sh check out: fd-200 flock at lines 13-14; viewer spawn (58-59) and setsid runService.sh fallback (159-160) lack 200>&- while the node spawn (78) has it, with the hazard documented in the script's own comment (73-74). Synthetic test proved the mechanism: a backgrounded python child inherits fd 200 (verified via /proc/<pid>/fd/200 and fuser), and after the supervisor is killed, a fresh 'exec 200>lock; flock -n 200' is denied — the lockout is real, and since the flock check (line 14) precedes restart_viewer's pkill (line 68/56), no future supervisor can self-heal. Refutations attempted and failed: bash does not set CLOEXEC on exec-opened fds; Python does not close inherited fds. runService.sh (./RoboticsServiceProcess & with no fd hygiene) propagates fd 200 into the setsid-detached daemon, supporting the permanent-lockout claim (confirmed for the shell chain; the final Qt binary closing inherited fds itself cannot be ruled out without running it, so that leg is plausible-leaning-confirmed). Scope caveats, not refutations: the live supervisor currently runs NO_VIEWER=1 (no viewer exists right now, accidental mitigation; default is viewer on), and the fallback only fires when systemctl --user restart fails — the current RoboticsServiceProcess is systemd-started with no fd 200. Minor addition: transient sleep 2/3 children also co-hold the lock (seen live via fuser) but die within seconds. Proposed fix (add 200>&- to line 59 and inside the subshell at line 160) is correct and sufficient.

confirmed.title: Grace re-arm misses the init-phase head_pose_ok state — recreates the documented 'unwinnable' 12 s kill loop
confirmed.detail: SEEN_DATA persists across node restarts (line 90 `SEEN_DATA=${SEEN_DATA:-0}` keeps the prior value), so after any session that ever saw data, a restarted node only gets the 12 s stall threshold unless line 119's re-arm fires. That re-arm greps only 'head_pose_dead\|timestamps FROZEN'. But in the very common recovery state 'link live, operator has not yet re-set Mode=Full-body', the node sits in init_xrt printing the head_pose_ok variant (node line 1027: 'app IS connected; no body data means Mode!=Full-body') which matches NEITHER pattern. Result: SEEN_DATA stays 1, THRESH stays 12 s, and the node is killed every 12 seconds while the operator needs 60-90 s to re-tick Mode — exactly the failure the 90 s grace comment (lines 116-118, 123-125) says was fixed. Combined with finding 2, each of those kills is a SIGKILL that leaks the SDK slot. Fix: also re-arm on 'head_pose_ok' when no body data has arrived this cycle, or reset SEEN_DATA=0 at the top of each node cycle.
confirmed.evidence: /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/scripts/run_rehearsal_supervised.sh:90, :116-126; /home/alois/full-body-teleoperation/HoloMotion/deployment/holomotion_teleop/holomotion_teleop_node.py:1026-1031 (message contains neither grep pattern).
confirmed.note: CONFIRMED after refutation attempts. (1) SEEN_DATA persists across node cycles: line 90 runs inside the outer respawn loop in the same shell, so a prior data-bearing session leaves SEEN_DATA=1 and THRESH=12s (line 126) for every restarted node. (2) Re-arm (line 119) greps only 'head_pose_dead|timestamps FROZEN'; the init-phase head_pose_ok message (node lines 1026-1031) matches neither, and during init the log contains only that diagnostic plus 'waiting for body data...' lines — no false re-arm source. (3) The scenario is real: main() calls init_xrt (line 1075) even with --skip-start-service; with app connected and headset worn, the head_pose_ok branch fires and no 'actual=...Hz' lines appear, so LAST_OK never updates and the node is killed every cycle (~17-20s wall per cycle, not exactly 12s: 12-15s detection + 3s TERM escalation + 2s respawn). NEW_PEER bounce does not rescue (Mode re-tick reuses the existing TCP session; a bounce wouldn't reset SEEN_DATA anyway); the service-recycle guard (lines 144-146) correctly stays hands-off but nothing stops the node kill loop. (4) STRONGER than claimed: the SIGKILL leak is independently verifiable, not dependent on finding 2 — install_stop_signal_handlers (node 385-394) only sets stop_event, which init_xrt's wait loop never checks (only main() line 1087, after init returns), so an init-phase node ignores SIGTERM and graceful_kill always escalates to kill -9 with no xrt.close(), leaking the single SDK client slot per the script's own comment (lines 20-23) — this is what makes the loop genuinely unwinnable. Bonus gap missed by the finding: the RUNTIME Mode-unset variant (node lines 157-161) also matches neither grep pattern; only the 'timestamps FROZEN' variant re-arms. Fix note: prefer the targeted re-arm on head_pose_ok-without-data; blanket SEEN_DATA=0 per cycle would grant 90s grace even after genuine mid-session stalls. Also worth fixing: make init_xrt's loop check stop_event so SIGTERM works during init.

confirmed.title: One malformed ZMQ packet permanently kills the reference subscriber thread (no restart)
confirmed.detail: ZmqReferenceSubscriber._run wraps the entire recv loop in a single try; any exception from _process_packet (topic-prefix mismatch, packet shorter than 1280B header, missing 'reference_qpos' field, corrupt JSON header, unsupported dtype) exits the loop and the thread never restarts — only one error line '[ZMQ] subscriber loop failed' is logged. The stream then looks permanently dead; during tracking the robot follows the frozen reference for up to max_data_age (1.5 s) then drops to velocity mode with no path back except a full node restart. Any stray or version-mismatched publisher reaching port 6001 can trigger this mid-run.
confirmed.evidence: HoloMotion/deployment/unitree_g1_ros2_29dof/src/humanoid_policy/reference_transport.py:312-324 (except Exception exits loop; finally closes socket; no respawn); staleness fallback at policy_runtime.py:428-433
confirmed.note: CONFIRMED with two corrections. Core claim verified against reference_transport.py:312-343: the recv loop is a single try; only zmq.Again is caught inline; any exception from _process_packet (line 321) reaches except Exception (322), logs one line '[ZMQ] subscriber loop failed' (324), and finally (325-343) closes socket/context — thread exits permanently. No respawn: subscriber is created/started once (policy_node_29dof.py:217,226), no is_alive monitoring, and _thread is never reset on crash so even a repeat start() would no-op. Fatal triggers verified reachable: packet < 1280B after topic (lines 81-84), corrupt JSON header (89), missing reference_qpos (258), unsupported dtype (98-99), field-exceeds-payload (105-109), plus empty frame_index array (IndexError at 262). Staleness fallback confirmed at policy_runtime.py:428-433; deployed profile launch_profiles/orin_docker.yaml:57 sets max_data_age: 1.5 (code default 0.6); re-entering motion mode via switch_to_motion_mode (line 241) immediately drops back since the buffer only ages — full node restart is the only recovery. Corrections: (1) the 'topic-prefix mismatch' trigger is effectively unreachable — the SUB socket subscribes to the same topic bytes (line 293) and ZMQ prefix-filters, so delivered packets always start with b'reference_qpos'; other triggers still stand. (2) 'Any stray publisher reaching port 6001' overstates exposure — the subscriber CONNECTs to a fixed endpoint (tcp://192.168.123.2:6001) where the teleop node binds (start_rehearsal.sh:16 binds tcp://*:6001); realistic vectors are a version/wire-format-mismatched teleop publisher, or a rogue process binding 6001 while the real one is down (SUB silently reconnects), and the payload must still carry the reference_qpos topic prefix. Severity and mechanism otherwise accurate.

confirmed.title: Stream-active fallback can inject stale motion-clip data into live teleop obs when kinematics is None
confirmed.detail: For ref_gravity_projection_cur/fut, ref_base_linvel_cur/fut, ref_base_angvel_cur/fut the branch ladder is: (1) stream active AND kinematics not None -> use live kinematics; (2) stream NOT active AND offline clip -> clip; (3) raw ref_raw_bodylink_* / ref_global_(angular_)velocity fallback with no stream check. If reference_stream_active is True but vr_reference.kinematics is None (update_kinematics skipped when has_future_sequence is momentarily false, or cleared after an exception at policy_runtime.py:455-474), branch 1 and 2 both fail and branch 3 serves data from whatever offline motion clip was loaded at startup, indexed by ref_motion_frame_idx — an unrelated clip's orientation/velocities silently replace the live reference for those 6 actor terms on that tick. If no clips are baked into the Orin install, the same state instead emits up to 6 unthrottled logger.warn calls per 50 Hz tick (log spam inside the control loop). Narrow window in practice (tracking entry is gated on seen_frames >= n_fut+delay+3), but it is the failure mode for any transient kinematics error mid-tracking.
